ledger.sentence: Magnetic resonance imaging, or MRI, uses strong magnetic fields and radio waves to take very detailed pictures from almost every angle.
ledger.note: KCH page text.

ledger.sentence: It does not use X-rays or other ionising radiation.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus: does not use ionizing radiation; NBT/UHS summary: scan itself does not use X-rays.

ledger.sentence: Coils placed around the part of the body being studied help to send and receive the radio waves and improve the quality of the pictures.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus: coils around the body part.

ledger.sentence: The person operating the scanner watches from another room.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus: operator watches from another room.

ledger.sentence: Scan length depends on the area examined, and NHS trust leaflets quote different times, from about 10 minutes to about 90 minutes.
ledger.note: Glos: 10 to 45 min; Chelsea and Westminster/Leeds: 15 to 90 min (summary of several trusts).

ledger.sentence: One trust says the total time in the department is likely to be about an hour.
ledger.note: Glos: total time about 60 minutes.

ledger.sentence: Staff settle the person on a couch that slides into the scanner.
ledger.note: Chelsea and Westminster: couch slides into scanner.

ledger.sentence: An intercom lets the person talk to the radiographer, and a call button is provided.
ledger.note: Chelsea and Westminster: intercom and call button.

ledger.sentence: The person is asked to keep still, because movement can blur the pictures.
ledger.note: Textbook-level; KCH/trust leaflets ask to lie still. Kept as textbook.

ledger.sentence: Some scans include an injection of contrast, a dye that helps to produce a more detailed picture and improves the accuracy of the scan.
ledger.note: Trust pages: contrast injection helps produce more detailed image and improves accuracy.

ledger.sentence: MedlinePlus says contrast is usually given through a vein, and that the most common agent contains gadolinium.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus: IV, gadolinium.

ledger.sentence: It adds that allergic reactions to this substance rarely occur.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus: allergic reactions rarely occur.

ledger.sentence: MedlinePlus also says gadolinium can be harmful for people with kidney problems who need dialysis, so kidney health is a standard question before a contrast scan.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus: gadolinium harmful to people with kidney problems requiring dialysis. US source.

ledger.sentence: The scanner makes loud beeping or hammering noises, so earplugs or headphones are provided and some departments play music.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus: loud beeping or hammering; Hampshire: earplugs/headphones, music.

ledger.sentence: MedlinePlus notes that some people feel claustrophobic, which means anxious in enclosed spaces.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus: patients may feel claustrophobic.

ledger.sentence: Trust leaflets say some people find the scan difficult for this reason.
ledger.note: Hampshire/NBT: some people find scans difficult.

ledger.sentence: They list options such as visiting the department beforehand, using a wider scanner, techniques that staff can use during the scan, or a mild sedative prescribed by a GP.
ledger.note: Hampshire/NBT/Newcastle summary: visit beforehand, wider-bore, staff techniques, GP-prescribed sedative.

ledger.sentence: A person who has a sedative needs someone to take them home afterwards.
ledger.note: Hampshire/NBT: sedative requires someone to take you home.

ledger.sentence: Before the scan each person completes a safety questionnaire.
ledger.note: York: patients complete a safety questionnaire; Barnsley summary.

ledger.sentence: York Hospitals says there are no known risks from an MRI scan when a person meets the safety standards.
ledger.note: York: 'no known risks if you meet the safety standards'.

ledger.sentence: The magnet can make pacemakers, artificial limbs and other implanted devices that contain metal malfunction or heat up, according to MedlinePlus.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus: magnet may cause pacemakers etc to malfunction or heat up.

ledger.sentence: Loose metal objects can be pulled toward the magnet and cause injury.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus: loose metal may cause injury if pulled toward magnet.

ledger.sentence: For that reason removable metal, such as jewellery and watches, comes off before the scan.
ledger.note: Barnsley/NBT summary: remove removable metal such as jewellery and watches.

ledger.sentence: Some implants, such as certain brain aneurysm clips or programmable shunts, may mean a scan cannot be done.
ledger.note: Barnsley/NBT summary.

ledger.sentence: Implants made of non-magnetic material are usually labelled MR safe or MR conditional, and some pacemakers can be scanned under strict conditions, according to a safety review.
ledger.note: PMC10657250 review: MR safe/conditional labels; pacemaker or ICD scanning with strict conditions.

ledger.sentence: Trust leaflets ask people to tell the imaging staff about any implants.
ledger.note: Barnsley/NBT summary.

ledger.sentence: MedlinePlus says tattoo dyes can irritate the skin or eyes, and medication patches can cause a skin burn.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus: tattoo dyes irritation; medication patches burn.

ledger.sentence: Usually no preparation is needed, and people can typically eat and drink as normal.
ledger.note: Royal Marsden/UHS summary.

ledger.sentence: Some scans of the abdomen or pelvis may need fasting for a few hours, and bowel-relaxing medicine is sometimes given.
ledger.note: Royal Marsden/UHS summary.

ledger.sentence: Results are not usually given on the day of the scan.
ledger.note: NBT: no results on the day.

ledger.sentence: A radiologist, a doctor who specialises in reading scans, studies the images and writes a report for the doctor who requested the scan.
ledger.note: KCH/York/NBT: radiologist studies images, writes report to referring doctor.

ledger.sentence: That doctor then discusses the findings with the person.
ledger.note: NBT: requesting clinician tells you.

ledger.sentence: The main extra risks come from the injection, as a small chance of a reaction to the contrast, and rare discomfort or tissue damage if the cannula, the small tube in the vein, leaks.
ledger.note: UHS/Chelsea/Royal Marsden: reaction to contrast; cannula leak.

ledger.sentence: Trouble breathing or swelling of the face after an injection would need a 999 call.
ledger.note: Textbook emergency signposting.

ledger.sentence: MRI uses strong magnetic fields and radio waves to take detailed pictures, and it does not use X-rays.
ledger.note: KCH: 'strong magnetic fields and radio waves'; MedlinePlus: 'does not use ionizing radiation'.

ledger.sentence: The scanner is loud, so earplugs or headphones are provided, and staff can talk to the person through an intercom.
ledger.note: Hampshire: loud, earplugs/headphones; Chelsea and Westminster: intercom and call button.

ledger.sentence: A safety questionnaire is completed first because some implanted devices can stop a scan from going ahead.
ledger.note: York: safety questionnaire, certain implanted devices may prevent a scan.

ledger.sentence: Results are not usually given on the day: a radiologist reports the images to the doctor who requested the scan.
ledger.note: NBT: no results on the day; radiologist reports to requesting clinician.

ledger.sentence: An MRI scan uses a strong magnet and radio waves, not X-rays, to take detailed pictures. This guide covers noise, safety checks, contrast and results.
ledger.note: Summary restates the supported sentences below.
